description: We're 6 students from UNMSM, Peru: 5 in Systems Engineering, 1 in Statistics, 8th semester. We combine software dev, data science, ML, and creative problem-solving under pressure (past hackathon/CTF experience). We want a solid, high-impact solution for NASA Space Apps while having fun. Looking for teammates with UI/UX skills, NASA API/satellite/geospatial data experience, or strong storytelling/pitching abilities.
summary:
MarsWalk Copilot is an AI-assisted mission planner for astronaut traverses on Mars. Astronauts on extravehicular activities must balance walking time, terrain slope, communications coverage, radiation exposure and scientific value at every stop, and today this is done manually with static maps. Our system turns it into a real-time optimization problem. 

A geospatial pipeline built from real NASA and USGS data of Jezero crater produces a cost graph of the terrain. An operations research engine computes optimal routes between eight real Perseverance waypoints. 

A local large language model lets the crew plan missions in plain language, asking for a route, relaxing a constraint or reacting to a dust storm alert, while every number is verified against the engine’s calculations.
details:
WHAT IT DOES?
MarsWalk Copilot plans astronaut traverses across the Jezero crater floor and delta on Mars. Given the stations to visit, a time budget and a maximum slope, it returns the optimal route with distance, time, peak slope, radiation dose index and communications coverage for each leg, plus the scientific reason each skipped station was omitted.

HOW IT WORKS
First, a data pipeline downloads the USGS SIM 3464 Jezero geologic map products (CTX stereo terrain model at 20 meters per pixel, THEMIS day and night thermal mosaics and geologic units), together with Perseverance waypoints and Navcam images.

Second, a route engine built as a FastAPI service uses Dijkstra for point-to-point routes and Google OR-Tools for multi-station missions, covering both route ordering and the team orienteering variant that maximizes scientific value within a time budget.

Third, a copilot runs on a local language model with five tools that call the engine’s API. It translates natural-language requests.

Fourth, a web frontend uses a MapLibre GL map with local elevation tiles and a Three.js 3D terrain viewer, station cards with real Navcam photography.

TOOLS USED
Python, FastAPI, NetworkX, Google OR-Tools, Ollama with Qwen2.5, React, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, Three.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Docker, Rasterio, PyProj, scikit-image and pytest.

BENEFITS
Every figure the crew sees is computed by verified algorithms and never invented by the AI, which is the core safety property for mission planning. The system works fully offline with a local model.

EXPECTED IMPACT
We hope to show that astronaut traverse planning can be treated as a real-time optimization problem with a conversational interface, without giving up numerical reliability.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE
The creative step is the separation of roles: the language model never computes, it only chooses among five tools and phrases their results, while an operations research engine produces every number.

FACTORS THE TEAM CONSIDERED

  • No invented numbers, and optimality tested against brute force.
  • Every parameter is labeled as NASA data, published formula.
  • A local offline model, plus a manual form that works without the language model.
  • Reliability of the code: automated tests for the engine and the verification layer.
